list.heading: Server migrations
list.subtitle: Move all the accounts of a registered server here: in parallel, with the source still serving, then cut over when you are ready.
list.emptyDescription: Register a server, read what it serves, then start a migration of its accounts.

form.heading: New server migration
form.subtitle: Choose a registered server whose accounts were read. Every account found becomes part of the migration; you map each to a plan and an owner next.
form.name: Name of the migration
form.bandwidth: Bandwidth limit in KiB per second (empty for none)
form.maranNote: This server is a Maran panel. Accounts are moved as packages: give the address of its pull endpoint, the key fingerprint you confirmed, and a pull grant for each account on the next screen.

errors.name: Enter a name.
errors.server: Choose a server with discovered accounts.
errors.concurrency: Enter a whole number from 1 to 8.
errors.bandwidth: Enter a whole number or leave it empty.
errors.maran: Enter the https address and the 64-character fingerprint.

limits.title: Limits
limits.description: Both apply while the migration runs: the number of accounts at once from the next account, the bandwidth from the next slice of every copy.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.noResultsDescription: No account has that name or domain.
accounts.map: Map to a plan and owner

dryRun.canStart: No conflicts. The migration can start.
dryRun.hasConflicts: There are conflicts. Names are never changed, so resolve each one on the source or leave the account out.

report.title: Report for {name}
report.converged: The final copy finished and the destination equals the source ({slices} runs).
report.notCopied: The files were moved as a package, not copied.
report.sourceBytes: Size of the source home: {bytes} bytes.
report.limit: The report states that the final copy converged. It is not a second measurement of the home on this server.

dns.title: DNS
dns.description: Where the migration's domains resolve now, read by this server.
dns.ttlAdvice: Lower the TTL of each record a day before the cut-over, point the records at this server after it, and keep the old copy until the new TTL has expired.

confirm.accountQuestion: The account created here for it is deleted again. Nothing on the source changes.
confirm.jobQuestion: Every account this migration created that is not yet cut over is deleted again. Accounts already cut over stay.

secrets.title: Generated passwords
secrets.intro: The source carries no passwords, so new ones were made. They are shown once and kept by nobody.
